The subject is a person with glasses and short hair, wearing a white shirt, holding the dark wooden instrument diagonally across their body. The metal bocal is in their mouth. In the background, there are black music stands and another woodwind instrument (likely a saxophone) on a stand to the left.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The musician's left hand (holding the lower part of the instrument) is severely malformed. The fingers appear fused into a single, smooth, fingerless mass or stump. There is no clear distinction between individual digits, and the connection to the wrist looks anatomically impossible.
The right hand fingers interacting with the keys lack clear definition. They seem to blend slightly into the keywork and each other, lacking distinct knuckles and nail beds.
The saxophone on the left appears overly smooth and lacks the detailed mechanical complexity (rods, springs, pads) expected of a real brass instrument, looking more like a simplified 3D model.
